newsitem.title: CANADA: Dia Met, BHP invited to ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Dia Met, BHP invited to ceremony.

text.p: Dia Met Minerals Ltd said Thursday that Canada's federal government had invited it and Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd to an "implementation protocol ceremony" Friday for their proposed Arctic diamond mine.
Asked if this meant the government had granted long-awaited final approval for the project, a Dia Met spokeswoman said, "It's very positive, that's what we're thinking."
The ceremony is to be held in Yellownife, the Northwest Territories.
Dia Met said the invitation was extended by Canada's Department of Indian and Northern Affairs.

The federal government gave approval in principle in August for the mine at Lac de Gras in the Northwest Territories. It said it hoped to grant final approval in early October once BHP had made significant progress toward striking agreements on sharing economic benefits with local residents and environmental monitoring.
Since then BHP has been in intense negotiations and has sealed several accords.

The diamond mine would be Canada's first. BHP had urged the government to grant final approval swiftly so it could ship construction materials to the site during the short winter season in which it is possible to reach the remote site by temporary road.
The project is expected to cost C$860 million by the time production starts in 1998.
Dia Met stock was halted. It last traded at 20.25, down 0.25, in Toronto.
